commits.title: An inventory of every reader of the site's null-store rows, as a script and a list that can only shrink

changes.how: A read-only Node script (node:fs, node:path, no dependencies). It walks src (files ending .ts or .tsx, not *.test.ts, not *.test.tsx) and prints, as JSON, one entry per file that matches any of these regular expressions, with the names of the patterns it matched: tables: /platform_theme_installs|platform_theme_install_updates|platform_page_roles|platformThemeInstalls|platformThemeInstallUpdates|platformPageRoles/ ; modules: /from "(@\/server\/|\.\/)(platform-theme-installs|platform-roles|platform-theme-preview)"|from "(@\/lib\/|\.\/)platform-roles"|from "(@\/components\/|\.\/)(platform-page|platform-layout)"/ ; chrome: /getPlatformChrome\(|siteLayoutFor\(null|textStylesCssFor\(null/ ; switch: /site_from_store|siteFromStore|siteStore\(/ . Output shape: { files: [{ file, patterns: [...] }], count }. With the argument `--write` it writes the same JSON to src/lib/null-site-readers.baseline.json, adding to each entry the field `kind` copied from the existing baseline when the file was already there, else "unclassed".

Run `node scripts/null-site-readers.mjs --write`, then set `kind` on every entry by reading the file: "site" (it serves or edits only the old site's pages, header, footer, menus or look: it will be deleted), "kept-route" (it serves a route the platform keeps: sign-up, get-domain, report, themes, status, support, unsubscribe, docs, the admin frame, the favicon and manifest: it will be moved to read the store), "switch" (it reads the switch platform_settings.site_from_store: the read goes when the old pages go). On 12 November 2026 the counts were: 7 files name platform_theme_installs, 4 name platform_page_roles, 8 name site_from_store, src/server/platform-navigation.ts has 43 importers and src/server/platform-roles.ts 14; getPlatformChrome() is called in 16 files.

Imports nothing from scripts; repeats the walk with the same four patterns (keep the patterns in one exported constant in scripts/lib/null-site-readers.mjs and import it from both the script and the test, as src/lib/await-deploy.test.ts imports a script's module). Two cases: (1) every file the walk finds is in the baseline (a new reader of the old site fails, with the message 'Kaizena Flow's site is its store's since D484: read the store, not the null-store rows'); (2) every baseline entry has a kind other than "unclassed". A file in the baseline that no longer matches does not fail: it tells the reader to run `node scripts/null-site-readers.mjs --write`.
Exports `PATTERNS` (the four named regular expressions above) and `readersIn(root)` (the walk). The script and the test both use it.
